text: {"claims":[{"claim_text":"Since Redis 7.0.0, the AOF is split into a base file and incremental files.","verdict":"SUPPORTED","reasoning":"Passage 0 explicitly states Redis uses a multi-part AOF mechanism in which the single AOF file is split into base and incremental files.","citations":[{"index":0,"quote":"Since Redis 7.0.0, Redis uses a multi part AOF mechanism. That is, the original single AOF file is split into base file (at most one) and incremental files (there may be more than one)."}]},{"claim_text":"There is at most one base file.","verdict":"SUPPORTED","reasoning":"Passage 0 directly states the base file is at most one.","citations":[{"index":0,"quote":"base file (at most one)"}]},{"claim_text":"There can be any number of incremental files.","verdict":"UNSUPPORTED","reasoning":"Passage 0 says there may be more than one incremental file, but it does not state that there can be any number of them.","citations":[]},{"claim_text":"All AOF files are tracked by a manifest file.","verdict":"SUPPORTED","reasoning":"Passage 0 states that all these files are tracked by a manifest file.","citations":[{"index":0,"quote":"All these files are put in a separate directory and are tracked by a manifest file."}]},{"claim_text":"The manifest file is written in JSON.","verdict":"UNSUPPORTED","reasoning":"None of the passages state the format of the manifest file.","citations":[]},{"claim_text":"During an AOF rewrite, the parent process opens a new incremental AOF file and continues writing to it.","verdict":"SUPPORTED","reasoning":"Passage 2 states the parent process opens a new incremental AOF file to continue writing during a scheduled rewrite.","citations":[{"index":2,"quote":"when an AOF rewrite is scheduled, the Redis parent process opens a new incremental AOF file to continue writing"}]},{"claim_text":"If an AOF rewrite fails, the old base and incremental files plus the newly opened incremental file still represent the complete updated dataset.","verdict":"SUPPORTED","reasoning":"Passage 7 directly states this failure case leaves a complete updated dataset.","citations":[{"index":7,"quote":"If the rewriting fails, the old base and increment files (if there are any) plus this newly opened increment file represent the complete updated dataset, so we are safe."}]},{"claim_text":"Failed AOF rewrites are retried at a slower and slower rate.","verdict":"SUPPORTED","reasoning":"Passage 2 states this as the purpose of the AOF rewrite limiting mechanism.","citations":[{"index":2,"quote":"Redis introduces an AOF rewrite limiting mechanism to ensure that failed AOF rewrites are retried at a slower and slower rate."}]},{"claim_text":"An AOF rewrite produces a new AOF with the minimal set of operations needed to recreate the current dataset.","verdict":"SUPPORTED","reasoning":"Passage 1 says a completely new file is produced with the minimal set of operations needed to create the current data set.","citations":[{"index":1,"quote":"a completely new one is produced with the minimal set of operations needed to create the current data set"}]},{"claim_text":"If the AOF is merely truncated at the end, Redis loads it by default.","verdict":"SUPPORTED","reasoning":"Passage 3 says recent Redis versions can load such an AOF, and passage 4 says the default configuration continues despite a malformed last command.","citations":[{"index":3,"quote":"The latest major versions of Redis will be able to load the AOF anyway, just discarding the last non well formed command in the file."},{"index":4,"quote":"the default configuration is to continue regardless of the fact the last command in the file is not well-formed"}]},{"claim_text":"When loading a truncated AOF, Redis discards the malformed last command.","verdict":"SUPPORTED","reasoning":"Passage 3 states Redis can load the AOF by discarding the last non-well-formed command.","citations":[{"index":3,"quote":"just discarding the last non well formed command in the file"}]},{"claim_text":"If the AOF is corrupted in the middle, Redis discards just the bad command and keeps going.","verdict":"CONTRADICTED","reasoning":"Passage 5 says mid-file corruption makes things more complex and Redis complains at startup and aborts, not that it keeps going after discarding only the bad command.","citations":[{"index":5,"quote":"If the AOF file is not just truncated, but corrupted with invalid byte sequences in the middle, things are more complex. Redis will complain at startup and will abort:"}]},{"claim_text":"Running redis-check-aof with --fix is always safe.","verdict":"CONTRADICTED","reasoning":"Passage 6 warns that using the utility to fix the file may discard everything from the invalid part to the end and can cause massive data loss.","citations":[{"index":6,"quote":"Otherwise it is possible to let the utility fix the file for us, but in that case all the AOF portion from the invalid part to the end of the file may be discarded, leading to a massive amount of data loss if the corruption happened to be in the initial part of the file."}]},{"claim_text":"redis-check-aof --fix only removes the invalid command.","verdict":"CONTRADICTED","reasoning":"Passage 6 says the fix may discard all AOF content from the invalid part to the end of the file, not only the invalid command.","citations":[{"index":6,"quote":"all the AOF portion from the invalid part to the end of the file may be discarded"}]}]}
